evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Scope and behavior are concrete (UI to create a game with name/description); a reasonable implementation estimate can be made.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Clear functionality (generate/share URL and access control) that can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Specific UI action and outcome; implementable and estimatable without detailed design.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Clearly scoped display requirement (list items for session) and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Concrete behavior (select item) that allows a reasonable estimate for implementation.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Straightforward CRUD operation; scope is not overly broad and is estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Specific edit operation; implementable and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Clear delete behavior with obvious acceptance; estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately ... even though not all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Behavior is specific (reveal estimates regardless of remaining estimators); can be reasonably estimated.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Computational requirement is clear (compute average) and implementable; estimation possible without detailed design.

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Specific trigger/action described; scope is narrow and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Simple input action with clear acceptance; implementable and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimation of prior item is a concrete behavior; scope is clear enough to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Import functionality is specific; while format details may be refined, reasonable estimates can be made (e.g., CSV/XLSX).

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Concrete interaction (paste into UI) with clear acceptance; estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing/listing requirement is clear and can be reasonably estimated.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Clear display requirement (transcript view); estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Specific export format (HTML) makes the task estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Specific export format (CSV) and straightforward acceptance criteria; estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Deletion and data removal is concrete; implementation and effort are estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: create an account ... entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Clear signup flow and required fields; estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Standard authentication behavior; scope clear enough to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Profile edit functionality is concrete; while which fields may vary, it is estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Account deletion with data removal is specific enough to estimate (may require cascade handling but not overly vague).

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Clear non-functional requirement (timezone conversion/display) and estimatable effort.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Standard password reset/email flow; behavior is concrete and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Specific option selection for card sets; scope is narrow and implementable.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Numeric limit specified; clear constraint makes estimation straightforward.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL
evaluations.rationale: Simple join flow clearly described and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Clear UI requirement (display the current item); estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Listing requirement similar to other stories; scope clear and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Concrete feedback requirement (indicator that someone has estimated); implementable and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Clear synchronization behavior (reveal when all have voted); estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Well-defined timing rule for changing estimates; scope is precise enough to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: be able to see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Requirement to show historical per-estimator estimates is concrete (data retrieval/display); estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Clear display requirement (associate estimates with users) and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: be able start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Specific timer behavior and visibility; implementable and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Specific trigger for timer reset; narrow scope and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: UI for navigating historical rounds is concrete and can be reasonably estimated.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Deterministic ordering requirement is specific and implementable; estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Timing-based edit permission is precise enough to estimate implementation effort.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Display of a thumbnail is concrete; implementation details (upload/source) can be scoped, so reasonable estimates are possible.

evaluations.evidence: have written a site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Non-functional quality goal is specific (standards compliance) and can be estimated (audit + remediation), though effort may vary.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Creating a glossary is a bounded task with definable scope; estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes, so that the queries run as fast as possible
evaluations.rationale: "as fast as possible" and which queries to index are unspecified; acceptance criteria are vague, making reasonable estimation difficult.

evaluations.evidence: have the application function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Specific list of target browsers/versions provides concrete scope; effort can be estimated though potentially large.

evaluations.evidence: have the site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is a known standard; though "where possible" adds some ambiguity, the work (audit + fixes) is estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: "Respond quickly" is vague (no measurable threshold) making it impossible to form a reliable implementation estimate.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Clear technical requirement (Unicode support) and implementable with estimatable effort.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design requirement is somewhat subjective but scoped enough to estimate routing/generation changes.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Creating user-friendly error pages is a bounded UI task; despite subjectivity of "nice", it is estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Anonymization/pseudonymization is a definable privacy task; while details matter, a reasonable estimate can be made (data model + anonymization approach).

evaluations.evidence: be able to see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: "Some metrics" is too vague (which metrics, granularity, presentation) and lacks acceptance criteria, preventing a reliable implementation estimate.
